text:
Matthew Knies was traded from Toronto to Columbus on September 28, the day before opening night, in the six-player deal that sent Kirill Marchenko to the Leafs. He scored twice in his Blue Jackets debut, then went quiet: The New York Times described his goal against Tampa Bay on November 12 as the end of a slump, in what was the Jackets' third straight loss. This week he goes back to Toronto.

The numbers explain the quiet. He has 4 goals and 9 points in 18 games, on exactly the 4.0 expected goals his chances deserved, but his chance rate has fallen from 0.94 expected goals per hour in Toronto last season to 0.73. His teammates have scored 3.1 fewer goals than expected with him on, which has cost him assists.

He's playing 18.25 minutes a night as a heavy top-six winger (33 hits), and Corey Sznajder's All Three Zones tracking noted that 18% of his setups come from behind the net, more than double a typical forward. Evolving-Hockey had him drawing the other team's best last season. Watch whether a bigger role in Columbus brings the chances back.
headline: Matthew Knies heads back to Toronto
